passages.text: Remember, O LORD, what has happened to us. Look and see our disgrace!
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel speak to the LORD.
They ask God to remember what happened to them.
They ask God to look at them.
They ask God to see their disgrace.
passages.original: זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ מֶֽה־ הָ֣יָה לָ֔נוּ הַבֵּיט וּרְאֵ֥ה אֶת־ חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel lost their inheritance.
Strangers took what belonged to them.
Foreigners now live in their houses.
The land and homes no longer belong to Israel.
passages.original: נַחֲלָתֵ֙נוּ֙ נֶֽהֶפְכָ֣ה לְזָרִ֔ים בָּתֵּ֖ינוּ לְנָכְרִֽים׃

passages.text: We have become fatherless orphans; our mothers are widows.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel speak in this passage.
They say they have become orphans.
They have no father.
Their mothers are like widows.
They have lost their protectors and providers.
passages.original: יְתוֹמִ֤ים הָיִ֙ינוּ֙ אֵין אָ֔ב אִמֹּתֵ֖ינוּ כְּאַלְמָנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: We must buy the water we drink; our wood comes at a price.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel lost their land and homes to foreigners.
They became poor and oppressed.
They must pay money for water to drink.
They must buy wood for use.
They cannot get water or wood freely.
They suffer under hardship and lack.
passages.original: מֵימֵ֙ינוּ֙ בְּכֶ֣סֶף שָׁתִ֔ינוּ עֵצֵ֖ינוּ בִּמְחִ֥יר יָבֹֽאוּ׃

passages.text: We are closely pursued; we are weary and find no rest.
passages.sermon:
We are closely pursued.
We feel constant pressure on our necks.
We are weary.
We find no rest.
passages.original: עַ֤ל צַוָּארֵ֙נוּ֙ נִרְדָּ֔פְנוּ יָגַ֖עְנוּ לֹא הֽוּנַ֖ח לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: We submitted to Egypt and Assyria to get enough bread.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel suffered hunger.
They needed food.
They reached out to Egypt for help.
They also reached out to Assyria for help.
They did this to have enough bread to eat.
passages.original: מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ נָתַ֣נּוּ יָ֔ד אַשּׁ֖וּר לִשְׂבֹּ֥עַֽ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: Our fathers sinned and are no more, but we bear their punishment.
passages.sermon: Our fathers sinned.\r\nOur fathers are gone.\r\nWe suffer for their sins.
passages.original: אֲבֹתֵ֤ינוּ חָֽטְאוּ֙ אֵינָם אֲנַחְנוּ עֲוֺנֹתֵיהֶ֥ם סָבָֽלְנוּ׃

passages.text: Slaves rule over us; there is no one to deliver us from their hands.
passages.sermon: Slaves rule over us.\r\nNo one can deliver us from their hands.
passages.original: עֲבָדִים֙ מָ֣שְׁלוּ בָ֔נוּ פֹּרֵ֖ק אֵ֥ין מִיָּדָֽם׃

passages.text: We get our bread at the risk of our lives because of the sword in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem suffer.
They try to find bread.
They risk their lives to get food.
Enemies attack them in the wilderness.
The sword threatens them as they search for bread.
passages.original: בְּנַפְשֵׁ֙נוּ֙ נָבִ֣יא לַחְמֵ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: Our skin is as hot as an oven with fever from our hunger.
passages.sermon:
We feel great hunger.
Our skin burns with heat.
Our skin feels as hot as an oven.
Hunger causes this burning fever.
passages.original: עוֹרֵ֙נוּ֙ כְּתַנּ֣וּר נִכְמָ֔רוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י זַלְעֲפ֥וֹת רָעָֽב׃

passages.text: Women have been ravished in Zion, virgins in the cities of Judah.
passages.sermon: Enemies attacked the women in Zion.\r\nThey violated the virgins in the cities of Judah.
passages.original: נָשִׁים֙ בְּצִיּ֣וֹן עִנּ֔וּ בְּתֻלֹ֖ת בְּעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Princes have been hung up by their hands; elders receive no respect.
passages.sermon:
Princes suffer greatly.
Enemies hang the princes by their hands.
People do not honor the elders.
Elders receive no respect.
passages.original: שָׂרִים֙ בְּיָדָ֣ם נִתְל֔וּ פְּנֵ֥י זְקֵנִ֖ים לֹ֥א נֶהְדָּֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Young men toil at millstones; boys stagger under loads of wood.
passages.sermon:
Young men work at millstones.
They carry heavy burdens.
Boys walk with loads of wood.
The loads are too heavy for them.
The boys stumble under the weight.
passages.original: בַּחוּרִים֙ טְח֣וֹן נָשָׂ֔אוּ וּנְעָרִ֖ים בָּעֵ֥ץ כָּשָֽׁלוּ׃

passages.text: The elders have left the city gate; the young men have stopped their music.
passages.sermon:
The elders have left the city gate.
The elders no longer sit in their place of honor.
The young men have stopped their music.
The young men no longer play or sing.
passages.original: זְקֵנִים֙ מִשַּׁ֣עַר שָׁבָ֔תוּ בַּחוּרִ֖ים מִנְּגִינָתָֽם׃

passages.text: Joy has left our hearts; our dancing has turned to mourning.
passages.sermon: Our hearts have lost their joy.\r\nOur dancing has become mourning.
passages.original: שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ לִבֵּ֔נוּ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ לְאֵ֖בֶל מְחֹלֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
passages.sermon: We have lost our crown.\r\nWe feel deep sorrow.\r\nWe have sinned.
passages.original: נָֽפְלָה֙ עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשֵׁ֔נוּ אֽוֹי־ נָ֥א לָ֖נוּ כִּ֥י חָטָֽאנוּ׃

passages.text: Because of this, our hearts are faint; because of these, our eyes grow dim— because of Mount Zion, which lies desolate, patrolled by foxes.
passages.sermon:
Our hearts feel weak.
Our hearts feel this way because of what has happened.
Our eyes grow dim.
Our eyes grow dim because of these troubles.
Mount Zion lies empty and ruined.
Foxes walk on Mount Zion.
Foxes walk there because the place is desolate.
passages.original: עַל־ זֶ֗ה הָיָ֤ה דָוֶה֙ לִבֵּ֔נוּ עַל־ אֵ֖לֶּה חָשְׁכ֥וּ עֵינֵֽינוּ׃ עַ֤ל הַר־ צִיּוֹן֙ שֶׁשָּׁמֵ֔ם שׁוּעָלִ֖ים הִלְּכוּ־ בֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: You, O LORD, reign forever; Your throne endures from generation to generation.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD reigns forever.
The LORD sits on His throne.
God’s throne lasts for all generations.
God’s rule never ends.
passages.original: אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֔ב כִּסְאֲךָ֖ לְדֹ֥ר וָדֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Why have You forgotten us forever? Why have You forsaken us for so long?
passages.sermon:
God, You are the Lord.
You reign forever.
Your throne lasts for every generation.
But now, we feel forgotten.
We feel left alone for a long time.
Why have You forgotten us forever?
Why have You left us for so many days?
passages.original: לָ֤מָּה לָנֶ֙צַח֙ תִּשְׁכָּחֵ֔נוּ תַּֽעַזְבֵ֖נוּ לְאֹ֥רֶךְ יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: Restore us to Yourself, O LORD, so we may return; renew our days as of old, unless You have utterly rejected us and remain angry with us beyond measure.
passages.sermon:
The people speak to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The people ask the LORD to bring them back to Him.
They want to return to the LORD.
They ask the LORD to make their days new again.
They want their days to be like they were before.
They say this unless the LORD has completely rejected them.
They say this unless the LORD is still very angry with them.
passages.original: הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ יְהוָ֤ה׀ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ וְנָשׁוּב חַדֵּ֥שׁ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כְּקֶֽדֶם׃ כִּ֚י אִם־ מָאֹ֣ס מְאַסְתָּ֔נוּ קָצַ֥פְתָּ עָלֵ֖ינוּ עַד־ מְאֹֽד׃
